question:
The values of \(y\) which will satisfy the equations

\[ \begin{aligned} 2x^2+6x+5y+1&=0,\\ 2x+y+3&=0 \end{aligned} \]

may be found by solving:
solution:
Because the choices are equations in \(y\) alone, use the linear equation to eliminate \(x\). From \(2x+y+3=0\),
\[
x=-\frac{y+3}{2}.
\]
Substitute this into \(2x^2+6x+5y+1=0\):
\[
\frac{(y+3)^2}{2}-3(y+3)+5y+1=0.
\]
Multiplying by \(2\) removes the denominator. Expanding and combining like terms gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
(y+3)^2-6(y+3)+10y+2&=0,\\
y^2+6y+9-6y-18+10y+2&=0,\\
y^2+10y-7&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
All steps are reversible: any root \(y\) of this equation, paired with \(x=-(y+3)/2\), satisfies both original equations. Thus the required equation is \(\boxed{y^2+10y-7=0}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
